newsitem.title: BULGARIA: IMF mission due in Sofia this month.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission due in Sofia this month.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission is expected to arrive in Bulgaria by the end of October to evaluate the country's reform performance and draft next year's budget frame, an IMF official said on Friday.
"The object of the mission is to reach agreement on a policy framework that would release the second tranche," IMF Sofia representative Franek Rozwadowski told Reuters.
It was not yet clear whether the mission would arrive next week or the week after, he said.
The IMF postponed a $115 million tranche last month until the government fulfilled its pledges to close down loss-making state enterprises and speed up privatisation.

The Socialist government said it would complete slow-moving closures of 64 loss-makers by end-October. It also announced plans to sell-off some 15 to 20 big state firms by year-end to boost its balance of payments.

If the Fund found Bulgaria's reform pace acceptable, Sofia stood to receive the second and the third tranche worth together some $180 million by year-end, said recently another IMF official who declined to be named.

The IMF mission is also expected to draft next year's macroeconomic frame jointly with the government, but drafting budget assumptions under current record high interest rates is unrealistic, economists say.
On Thursday, Bulgaria's central bank cut the central interest rate to 240 percent from an all-time high of 300 percent in a bid to ease lending to the stagnant economy.

The central bank imposed the shockingly high rates in a bid to stabilise the slumping lev and curb inflation. The lev has firmed to around 220 to the dollar this week from 235 in mid-September, when the rate was hiked.
September consumer price inflation stood at 18.8 percent.
Bulgarian officials have said that it was important to win external funding by year-end as the first big foreign debt payments of $170 million were due in January.

Central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov said in a newspaper interview this week that he hoped that quick sell-offs would boost foreign exchange reserves by up to $400 million. Bulgaria's forex reserves stood at $506 million in September. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
